verdicts.rationale: The introduction explicitly links sparsity, filamentous morphology, noise, and limited sliding-window receptive fields to segmentation difficulty and fragmentation.
The workflow specifies global inspection, regional instructions, tool editing, validation, and both stated termination conditions.
Equation 2 uses global and local mask projections and Betti numbers; the text defines these as 3D connected-component counts and assigns FP/FN labels.
The advisor jointly analyzes orthogonal image/mask projections and specifies location and operation in each instruction.

The main method explicitly describes both checks, instruction regeneration, and human escalation. The claim appropriately limits its attribution to that description; the supplementary prompt also permits unchanged topology.
The architecture description specifies concatenated image/mask encoding, frozen text encoding, deepest-feature cross-attention, and mask decoding.
The training description distinguishes synthetic perturbations with derived instructions from real prediction errors with Qwen3-VL instructions.
The dataset description confirms the benchmarks, prior splits, BigNeuron diversity, and all stated CWMBS counts, dimensions, and resolution.
The dataset description gives the stated imaging modality, larval age, volume dimensions, and physical resolution.
The second-stage details explicitly list the five networks, selection metrics, 5,310 volumes, and their dimensions.
The experimental details state all four configurations exactly as claimed.
Table 2 confirms the three F1 values; their differences are 13.19 and 3.02 percentage points. The accompanying text confirms initialization.
All six numerical values match Table 2, and the text identifies 3D U-Net outputs as initialization.
Table 1 confirms both baseline F1 values and all four refinement results under the corresponding initialization and subset.
Table 3 supplies the stated F1 values, and the ablation description identifies the no-agent condition as indiscriminate refinement of all blocks.
The ablation reports exactly these rejection-rate and F1 changes for real-defect training from scratch versus the two-stage strategy.
The limitations describe depth loss in dense regions, and the inspector ablation discusses interference from overlapping neurons.
The contributions explicitly make this novelty claim and introduce the editing tool and two-stage training; the wording correctly attributes novelty to the authors.
The conclusion states refinement without agent training, while the method states diagnostic decisions and instructions are auditable.
